title: Find safe land and natural resources
short: Local hazards, soil, water sources, wild plants and finding your way
intro: A learning track for understanding the ground you live on: which natural hazards threaten it, whether its soil and water can be used, why wild plants need great caution, and how to read maps and navigate. The app's separate offline Maps page shows places; this track explains what the map data can and cannot tell you.

limits.text: Surface water from rivers, streams, lakes and ponds is often contaminated and should not be drunk unless treated first.
Roofs made of lead, asbestos or tar contain toxic chemicals that make collected rainwater unsafe to drink.
There is no field test to tell if an unknown mushroom is edible; some wild mushrooms are hard even for experts to identify.
Many poisonous plants look like edible ones; boiling removes many poisons but not all.
Some earthquake strengthening projects can be done yourself, but others may need a contractor, architect or engineer.
In a tsunami warning, go to high ground as far inland as possible and do not wait.
Former industrial sites and old gas stations may need expert help to assess soil before use.
